      "title": "Async legacy writes use request-scoped context and will be canceled",
      "body": "In Create, the goroutine derives its context from the method's ctx parameter, which is typically the HTTP request context. Once the handler returns, this context is canceled, causing the legacy write (Legacy.Create) to fail or be interrupted before completion. The same pattern is used in Delete (line 110), Update (line 135), and DeleteCollection (line 163). The intended async 'safe measure' write to legacy will almost always be aborted because the request context is canceled when the response is sent. The goroutine should use a context detached from the request, such as context.Background() or a context with a timeout but no request cancellation."

This records the failed unified storage operation as a legacy operation, polluting metrics used to monitor legacy write behavior. It should call d.recordStorageDuration instead."

This mislabels the failed unified storage update as a legacy operation. Metrics for storage failures will be missing, and legacy metrics will be incorrectly incremented. It should record storage duration."

This records the legacy operation as if it were a unified storage operation, corrupting both storage and legacy metrics. It should call d.recordLegacyDuration."

Other methods pass options.Kind. This will cause storage duration metrics to be split by object name, creating a high-cardinality label and making the metric useless for aggregation by kind.       "body": "In doPlaylistTests, after creating playlists via the Kubernetes API (which in mode 3 triggers an asynchronous legacy write), the test immediately performs a legacy API list request and expects the newly created playlists to be present. Because the legacy write is asynchronous and may not have completed, the test is prone to flakiness. A wait mechanism or retry loop should be added to ensure the legacy write has propagated before asserting."

      "line": 65,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Unit tests for mode 3 do not wait for async legacy writes",
      "body": "The unit tests for Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection call the dual writer and then return without waiting for the asynchronous goroutine that writes to legacy storage to complete. This can lead to: (1) the legacy mock not being called before the test ends, so the test does not actually verify that legacy write happens; (2) a potential data race if the mock is used by the goroutine after the test has finished or while other tests are using the shared mock; (3) leaked goroutines that may run after test completion. The tests should synchronize with the goroutine (e.g., using a sync.WaitGroup or a channel) before asserting on the mock or returning."

findings.title: Async legacy writes use request-scoped context and will be canceled
findings.body: In Create, the goroutine derives its context from the method's ctx parameter, which is typically the HTTP request context. Once the handler returns, this context is canceled, causing the legacy write (Legacy.Create) to fail or be interrupted before completion. The same pattern is used in Delete (line 110), Update (line 135), and DeleteCollection (line 163). The intended async 'safe measure' write to legacy will almost always be aborted because the request context is canceled when the response is sent. The goroutine should use a context detached from the request, such as context.Background() or a context with a timeout but no request cancellation.

findings.title: Create error path records legacy duration instead of storage duration
findings.body: When d.Storage.Create returns an error, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). This records the failed unified storage operation as a legacy operation, polluting metrics used to monitor legacy write behavior. It should call d.recordStorageDuration instead.

findings.title: Update error path records legacy duration instead of storage duration
findings.body: When d.Storage.Update returns an error, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). This mislabels the failed unified storage update as a legacy operation. Metrics for storage failures will be missing, and legacy metrics will be incorrectly incremented. It should record storage duration.

findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy write records storage duration instead of legacy duration
findings.body: Inside the goroutine that writes to Legacy.DeleteCollection, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). This records the legacy operation as if it were a unified storage operation, corrupting both storage and legacy metrics. It should call d.recordLegacyDuration.

findings.title: Delete success storage duration uses object name as kind label
findings.body: In the success path of Delete, the call d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) passes the object name as the 'kind' argument. Other methods pass options.Kind. This will cause storage duration metrics to be split by object name, creating a high-cardinality label and making the metric useless for aggregation by kind. It should use options.Kind like other paths.

findings.title: Integration test checks legacy API immediately after async legacy write
findings.body: In doPlaylistTests, after creating playlists via the Kubernetes API (which in mode 3 triggers an asynchronous legacy write), the test immediately performs a legacy API list request and expects the newly created playlists to be present. Because the legacy write is asynchronous and may not have completed, the test is prone to flakiness. A wait mechanism or retry loop should be added to ensure the legacy write has propagated before asserting.

findings.title: Unit tests for mode 3 do not wait for async legacy writes
findings.body: The unit tests for Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection call the dual writer and then return without waiting for the asynchronous goroutine that writes to legacy storage to complete. This can lead to: (1) the legacy mock not being called before the test ends, so the test does not actually verify that legacy write happens; (2) a potential data race if the mock is used by the goroutine after the test has finished or while other tests are using the shared mock; (3) leaked goroutines that may run after test completion. The tests should synchronize with the goroutine (e.g., using a sync.WaitGroup or a channel) before asserting on the mock or returning.
